diagnosis.summary: Flink job `events-to-iceberg` restarted ~2 minutes ago (TaskExecutor shutdown), causing ~2 checkpoint failures that triggered the alert. The job is already back RUNNING/STABLE and completing checkpoints normally; this appears to be a Chaos Mesh-induced disruption.
diagnosis.root_cause: The Flink TaskExecutor was forcibly shut down approximately 1.9 minutes ago (K8s event: `org.apache.flink.util.FlinkExpectedException: The TaskExecutor is shutting down`), causing the job to restart and in-flight checkpoints to fail. The restart correlates with a `chaos-mesh-local` deployment 27–31 minutes ago — a pattern that also explains a mass pod-kill event (exit code 255 / Unknown) across Kafka brokers, the Flink JobManager and ingestion-service ~140 minutes ago, which coincided with an earlier chaos-mesh deployment 144 minutes ago. The checkpoint failures are a direct side-effect of the restart, not an independent storage or coordination issue. The job has since recovered: 24.995 completed checkpoints in the last 5 minutes at the expected 10-second interval, Kafka is fully healthy (0 under-replicated/offline partitions), and all 3 nodes across all zones are Ready.
diagnosis.impact: Approximately 2 checkpoints failed during the ~90-second restart window. Exactly-once delivery was preserved via the last successful checkpoint. Consumer lag is 650 messages and catching up. No data loss expected; brief delay in Iceberg data visibility during restart.

evidence.finding: Job RUNNING/STABLE, uptime 96s, restarts_last_15m=1.018, failed_checkpoints_last_10m=2.104, completed_checkpoints_last_5m=24.995. New taskmanager pod age=1.9 min. Consumer lag=650.
Warning JobException on FlinkDeployment/events-to-iceberg 1.9 min ago: 'The TaskExecutor is shutting down' (org.apache.flink.util.FlinkExpectedException).

chaos-mesh-local redeployed at 27 and 31 minutes ago (revision 2.8.5,47886843e767 and 2.8.5,c702990f596b). An earlier chaos-mesh deployment 144 minutes ago preceded mass pod kills (exit 255/Unknown) on all Kafka brokers, Flink JM, and ingestion pods at ~140.9 minutes ago.
All apps pods Running/Ready. events-to-iceberg-taskmanager-2-2 is brand new (1.9 min old). JM last terminated 140.9 min ago with exit 255/Unknown; re-started 139.4 min ago.
All 3 Strimzi brokers Ready, 0 under-replicated partitions, 0 under-min-ISR, 0 offline partitions. Cluster status=True/Ready.
All 3 worker nodes Ready across zone-a, zone-b, zone-c. No pressure conditions or cordons.

proposed_action.rationale: The Flink job is already RUNNING/STABLE and completing checkpoints at the normal rate (≈25 per 5 min). The checkpoint failures were transient, caused by the restart itself. No manual intervention is needed; the job is self-healing. Restarting the Flink job would only introduce another checkpoint disruption.

follow_ups: Confirm whether the Chaos Mesh deployment 27 minutes ago intentionally targeted the Flink TaskManager (check Chaos Mesh CRs / experiment schedules). If unintentional, roll back or disable the experiment.
Monitor consumer lag (currently 650) over the next 5–10 minutes to confirm the job is catching up.
Investigate why all pods (Kafka, Flink, ingestion) terminated with exit code 255 / 'Unknown' ~140 minutes ago — if that was also a Chaos Mesh experiment, ensure it is complete and not repeating.
Loki and Prometheus data sources returned errors during investigation; verify observability stack health (OpsAgentInvestigationsFailing alert is also firing for 54 minutes).
The iceberg-exporter pod had readiness probe failures 27.6 minutes ago — verify it is fully healthy and Iceberg table metrics are accurate.
